title: Derivative kick and setpoint weighting
physicalPurpose: Move the loaded table without allowing a setpoint discontinuity to create an unsafe motor-torque request.
principalTechnique: Derivative setpoint weighting and derivative on measurement
objective: Expose derivative kick, distinguish requested from applied torque, and select derivative on measurement without removing motion damping.

simplifications: The four-newton-metre gravity coefficient produces angle-dependent torque G*sin(position), not a constant disturbance.
The setpoint changes instantaneously so derivative kick is isolated and measurable.
Encoder noise remains absent until Lesson 23.

baseline.limitation: Differentiating the full setpoint step creates a requested torque above 70 N m even though the drive can apply only 10 N m.

change.decision: Select c equal to zero only if the initial requested torque is at most 5 N m, applied torque remains bounded, and final position still tracks within 0.02 rad.

disturbances: Angle-dependent payload gravity G*sin(position) with G equal to 4 N m throughout every run

abortPredicates: Position, velocity, requested torque or applied torque is nonfinite
Applied torque leaves -10 to 10 N m
safety.restorationMode: Manual with zero torque after mechanically supporting the payload
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The deliberately discontinuous setpoint shall not be applied to a physical axis without independent motion-profile and drive-limit review.

video.viewerOutcome: Explain derivative kick, distinguish controller request from drive output, and justify derivative on measurement from recorded evidence.

learning.context: The loaded positioning table uses the PID gains from Lesson 21, but an instantaneous setpoint change now exposes the derivative path's command response.
learning.reason: Integral action removed load error, yet derivative on the full error turns a setpoint discontinuity into a very large requested torque.
theory: The derivative setpoint weight c is a dimensionless value from zero to one that chooses how much setpoint motion enters the derivative path.
The weighted derivative input x_D equals c times SP minus PV. Its change divided by elapsed time dt is multiplied by derivative gain Kd to form derivative torque.

At c one, the full setpoint step enters the derivative calculation. At c zero, only measured PV motion enters, so a command step alone creates no derivative kick. An intermediate c retains part of the kick.
Requested motor torque T_requested is the PID calculation before the physical drive clamp. Applied motor torque T_applied is the bounded torque that reaches the plant; both must remain visible.
Derivative on measurement still responds to real table motion and therefore preserves the damping purpose from Lesson 20.
learning.workedPrediction: A 0.5 rad setpoint step over 0.02 s has apparent rate 25 rad/s. With Kd 3, c 1 requests about 75 N m derivative torque, c 0.5 about 37.5 N m, and c 0 none; the proportional path adds about 4 N m before the drive clamps applied torque to 10 N m.
practicalPreparation: Confirm the project-owned 0 to 0.5 rad step, 20 ms cycle, sine-gravity law with 4 N m peak coefficient, plus or minus 10 N m physical drive limit, wide diagnostic controller-request range and supported-payload restoration.
learning.baseline: Run c equal to one and retain the first requested and applied torque samples after the setpoint step together with the position response.
learning.change: Restore identical conditions and repeat with c equal to 0.5 and then zero; change no gain, plant, event, timing, limit or seed.
learning.comparison: Compare first post-step requested torque, applied torque and the full position response for all three weights on equal scales.
learning.validation: Require c one request at least 70 N m, c 0.5 at least 30 N m above c zero, c zero request at most 5 N m, every applied torque within plus or minus 10 N m and c zero absolute SP-minus-PV error at the 15-second final sample at most 0.02 rad; do not present that endpoint as steady-state evidence.
learning.explanation: Explain why removing SP from the derivative input prevents a mathematical command discontinuity from becoming a torque kick while measured physical motion still produces damping torque.
learning.transfer: Derivative on measurement is a robust default for command-following loops, but measured encoder noise is still differentiated; Lesson 23 adds and qualifies filtering.
